findings.title: Recommendations omit required structured provenance
findings.what: Each returned recommendation makes measured or causal claims but supplies no provenance object identifying the source artifact and fields needed to reproduce them. The rework and runaway detectors additionally characterize correlations as retry storms/unbounded loops without evidence proving those causes.
findings.fix: Add claimClass/proofTier and structured provenance observations citing the exact parsed fields and values. Restrict rework/runaway wording to the measured churn or token-outlier facts unless causal proof is available.
findings.acceptance: For each detector, a firing fixture passes the repository provenance validator; observations identify the relevant source fields and values; tests assert the arithmetic; and rework/runaway details no longer claim an unproven cause.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed all four return objects omit provenance entirely. The unsupported causal wording remains at rework-signature.ts:51-59 and runaway-workflow-cost.ts:92-95; no comparison-only file is included.

findings.title: Default-validated CLAUDE.md fixes interpolate untrusted artifact text
findings.what: Both fixes omit fixKind, making them validated/copy-paste-safe by default, yet construct Markdown from parsed filenames or command text. Newlines, backticks, Markdown directives, or CLAUDE.md instructions in those values are not escaped; the redundant-read fix also emits ambiguous basenames while telling the user to replace them before use.
findings.fix: Mark these dynamic templates illustrative, or strictly encode/validate artifact text and emit unambiguous repo-relative paths so the resulting snippet is safe verbatim.
findings.acceptance: Adversarial fixtures containing newline/backtick/instruction text cannot alter the snippet structure; effectiveFixKind is illustrative unless the emitted content is demonstrably safe and immediately usable; fix-validity assertions cover both detectors.
findings.verifyNote: Second-pass inspection confirmed raw basename interpolation at redundant-reads.ts:96-102 and raw command interpolation at repeated-commands.ts:34-46, with no fixKind in either returned fix. Their user-facing notes also show adaptation is required, contradicting validated semantics.

findings.title: Historical review snapshots retain present-tense bottleneck claims
findings.what: generatedAt is converted into provenance.asOf, but its age is never compared with now and title/detail/inference always say the queue is currently bottlenecked and requests are pending. A stale synchronized snapshot therefore produces an outdated operational recommendation as if current.
findings.fix: Compute dataset freshness from generatedAt, mark stale provenance, and prefix/demote title or detail to 'As of YYYY-MM-DD' when outside a documented freshness window; alternatively suppress unusably old snapshots.
findings.acceptance: A test with an old generatedAt produces an explicit 'As of <date>' historical claim and provenance.stale=true (or returns null), while a fresh fixture preserves current-tense wording.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read verified generatedAt only feeds asOf at lines 176-178 and 237. No freshness branch exists before the unconditional present-tense title/detail at lines 196-199.

findings.title: Session opener clustering is unbounded quadratic work
findings.what: For every project, clusterProject executes all n(n−1)/2 opener pairs and performs a set-based Jaccard comparison for each. There is no cap, time-bucket index, candidate index, probe, or budget, so large session histories can create quadratic recommendation latency and CPU use.
findings.fix: Sort/index records by timestamp and similarity candidates, compare only records inside the seven-day window, and add a documented input/latency budget or safe cap.
findings.acceptance: A benchmark or probe over a documented large-history fixture stays within the chosen latency budget and demonstrates candidate comparisons growing sub-quadratically for sparse real-world histories without changing detector results.
findings.verifyNote: Second-pass inspection confirmed the nested loops at lines 254-257 cover every pair before similarity filtering; the seven-day check avoids Jaccard work but does not avoid pair enumeration, and no bound exists in the surrounding record or project grouping code.
